reel.caption:
Can one investment pay you every month? | SWP Explained

A Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) takes a fixed amount out of your mutual fund every month, straight to your bank account. The rest stays invested.
Illustrative: ₹10 lakh, ₹6,000 a month for 10 years, assuming 8% a year. You take out ₹7.2 lakh and about ₹10.8 lakh is still left. Returns are not guaranteed: in a bad market year the balance falls, and a withdrawal bigger than the fund's growth eats into your own money.
Tax: each withdrawal sells units, and only the profit part is taxed, not the full amount (equity funds held over 12 months: 12.5% on yearly long-term gains above ₹1.25 lakh; under 12 months: 20%; debt funds bought after 1 Apr 2023: your slab).

Save this for later.

Sources: an asset manager's tax guide (updated Jun 2026) and a broker's personal-finance news explainer (updated Nov 2025), which agree on the tax rules. ₹ figures calculated: monthly compounding at an assumed 8% a year, withdrawal at the end of each month, before tax.
